# Headline

The procedure is written and all three notes files now pass the check tool.

1. The procedure file notes/procedure.md gives seven numbered steps any agent can follow.
2. Each of the three notes files keeps its meaning after the fix.
3. The check tool reports zero failures on all four files after the fix.

## Background

The task asked for a reusable procedure, then for fixes to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md in that order. The check tool flags banned words and sentences over 25 words.

## Relevance

A shared procedure means future notes files get the same fix with the same standard.

## Information

First, the procedure went into notes/procedure.md. Then the fixes followed it per file:

- notes/a.md: removed the banned word "clearly". The sentence count stayed the same. Check now passes.
- notes/b.md: split one 45-word sentence into three sentences. Check now passes.
- notes/c.md: removed the banned word "very". Split one 38-word sentence into three short sentences. Check now passes.

The final check on all four files shows zero long sentences and zero banned words. The check tool output is the measurement for each file. [P]

Alternative considered: rewriting each file more freely. This loses because the task requires keeping the meaning of each file, so minimal edits are safer [judgment].

No assumptions were made, since the check tool defines both failure types.

## End

I recommend that we

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the shared fix procedure. This is deterministic and Clear, since the tool output (P) decides each step. Test: Given a notes file with issues, When an agent follows the steps, Then the check tool reports zero failures.
2. Run the check tool on all notes files whenever one changes. This is deterministic and Clear. Test: Given any edited notes file, When the check tool runs, Then failures appear before the file is accepted.

# Fix banned words and long sentences in a notes file

1. Run the check tool on the target file to get the list of banned words and sentences over 25 words.
2. If no issues are reported, stop and move to the next file.
3. For each banned word, remove it or replace it with a plain word that keeps the meaning.
4. For each sentence over 25 words, split it into two or more short sentences that keep the original meaning.
5. Write the fixed content back to the file in full.
6. Run the check tool again on the file.
7. If issues remain, repeat steps 3 to 6. Otherwise the file is done.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It writes the result to the store. It then marks the message as done, so no other worker picks it up again.
